items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: AC1-AC4 implemented and proven end-to-end against this repo's own tree (F0 GREEN, 87% diff-coverage, real structural drift correctly detected as exit 1); AC5/AC6 docs and SPEC/brief status notes done. One documented divergence from the SPEC's original 'failt hart' framing: the compare step is advisory-only, exactly as decided during plan-review (both external reviewers flagged the naive hard-gate as false-red-prone on the very first PR) and recorded in the SPEC's own P0a status note.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: Every external call (git show, subprocess uv run, file reads) raises a typed error (DriftCheckError/StageError/ManifestError) on failure; nothing is silently swallowed. ci_manifest_drift_check.py's own three-step orchestration returns EXIT_ERROR (2) on any pre-comparison failure, never falling through to a false-clean comparison.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No SQL/HTML (n/a, no web routes). stage_f0_evidence.py explicitly guards path traversal (report_path must resolve beneath the run directory) and rejects duplicate unit ids. All subprocess calls use fixed argv with shell=False (nosec-annotated). No secrets in source.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: 49 new/edited unit tests assert on outcomes (exit codes, staged file contents, manifest diffs) not internals; each new tool has a happy path plus every documented failure mode, plus a real-subprocess CLI smoke test added specifically to catch the sys.path-masking bug class this same build caught and fixed in three files.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: No N+1 patterns. Retention writes once per unit during the run it already executes; pruning caps retained runs at 5. ci.yml's plan/verify/drift-check steps each run once per job, not per test root.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: New files sit under shared/scripts/tools and shared/scripts/lib, matching the existing convention; all are under 300 lines except run_test_suite.py (pre-existing ADR-123 exception, baseline refreshed 518->529 and verified against the anti-ratchet gate).

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: touches_io_boundary applies (extensive json.dump/json.load across the new tools). Producer/consumer pairs and their round-trip tests: ci_junit_plan.py plan -> plan.json -> {lookup, verify, ci.yml jq lookups, ci_manifest_drift_check.py's stage_ci_reports} (test_ci_junit_plan.py write_plan->lookup/verify); suite_retention.py Retention.publish() -> manifest.json side-manifest -> stage_f0_evidence.py (test_suite_retention.py record->publish->read, test_stage_f0_evidence.py full round trip via real Retention fixtures); compare_traceability_manifest.py's own committed/regenerated manifest pair, proven against a REAL regeneration of this repo's own tracked manifest in the full local proof run, not just synthetic fixtures. None of these are user-edited formats, so the 8-probe boundary-probes.md checklist (aimed at hand-edited configs) does not apply verbatim; the round-trip coverage above is the applicable substitute.
